purpose: Grind coffee beans to produce ground coffee with consistent particle size

inputs.name: bean_flow
inputs.description: Rate of coffee beans entering the grinder

outputs.name: grind_consistency
outputs.description: Grind consistency reported as a percentage (state * 100)

states.name: burr_health
states.description: Burr health index, 1.0 = new, 0.0 = worn out; wear accelerates as health drops

states.name: grind_consistency
states.description: Grind consistency, 1.0 = fully consistent; degrades with burr wear

events.name: burr_replacement_needed
events.description: Burrs worn below the replacement threshold

events.name: grinder_blocked
events.description: The grinder may be blocked or damaged

state_transition_logic: burr_health decreases by base_wear_rate * bean_flow * (1 + wear_acceleration_factor * (1 - burr_health)) * dt, clamped to [0.0, 1.0]
grind_consistency decreases by grind_degradation_rate * (1 - burr_health)^1.5 * dt, clamped to [0.0, 1.0]
event_logic: burr_replacement_needed: event_state = (burr_health - replacement_threshold) / (1 - replacement_threshold), clamped to [0, 1]
grinder_blocked: event_state = (grind_consistency - blockage_threshold) / (1 - blockage_threshold), clamped to [0, 1]
assumptions: Ceramic burrs wear gradually with use, reducing grinding consistency
Bean flow rate directly correlates with burr wear accumulation
Grinding efficiency is proportional to burr condition
Hopper issues manifest after significant burr wear
Blockages occur when grinding consistency falls below operational threshold
Spec synced to hand-edited component code (2026-05-28) so spec and code agree.
